```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
```

**Primary Research Question:** Can we predict which adults are likely to be hospitalized based on their demographic characteristics, health status, chronic conditions, and healthcare utilization patterns?

# Data Description

The analysis integrates five types of MEPS data files:

1. **Longitudinal Files (Panels 6-10)** - Person-level consolidated data including demographics, insurance coverage, health status, and utilization summaries
2. **Medical Condition Files (2001-2006)** - ICD-9 diagnosis codes used to identify chronic conditions and exclude cancer patients
3. **Prescribed Medicine Files (2001-2006)** - Prescription records used to calculate medication counts and polypharmacy status
4. **Inpatient Stay Files (2001-2006)** - Hospital admission records
5. **Emergency Room Files (2001-2006)** - ER visit records

## Functions for Loading MEPS Data

MEPS data files are distributed in fixed-width format, where each variable occupies specific character positions. The following functions parse the SAS programming statements files to determine column positions, then load the data accordingly.

```{r load-functions}
# Parse SAS input statements to extract variable positions
get_var_positions <- function(sas_file) {
  
  lines <- readLines(sas_file, warn = FALSE)
  
  # Variable definitions start with @ followed by position number
  pos_lines <- lines[grep("^\\s*@\\d+", lines)]
  
  vars <- data.frame(
    name = character(),
    start = integer(),
    width = integer(),
    type = character(),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  for (line in pos_lines) {
    # Pattern: @position variable_name $optional width
    parts <- regmatches(line, regexec("@(\\d+)\\s+(\\w+)\\s*(\\$)?\\s*(\\d+)", line))[[1]]
    
    if (length(parts) >= 5) {
      vars <- rbind(vars, data.frame(
        name = parts[3],
        start = as.integer(parts[2]),
        width = as.integer(parts[5]),
        type = ifelse(parts[4] == "$", "c", "d"),
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      ))
    }
  }
  
  return(vars)
}

# Load MEPS fixed-width data file using parsed positions
read_meps_file <- function(dat_file, sas_file) {
  
  var_info <- get_var_positions(sas_file)
  
  if (nrow(var_info) == 0) {
    stop("Could not parse variable definitions from SAS file")
  }
  
  col_pos <- fwf_positions(
    start = var_info$start,
    end = var_info$start + var_info$width - 1,
    col_names = var_info$name
  )
  
  df <- read_fwf(
    dat_file,
    col_positions = col_pos,
    col_types = paste(var_info$type, collapse = ""),
    progress = FALSE
  )
  
  return(df)
}
```

## Create Chronic Condition Flags

Using ICD-9 diagnosis codes from the condition files to create binary flags for major chronic conditions. The code ranges are based on standard ICD-9-CM classifications.

```{r chronic-conditions}
# Function to extract numeric ICD-9 category code
get_icd_num <- function(code) {
  if (is.na(code)) return(NA)
  cleaned <- gsub("[^0-9]", "", substr(as.character(code), 1, 3))
  if (cleaned == "") return(NA)
  return(as.numeric(cleaned))
}

# Create condition flags for each person based on their diagnoses
chronic_flags <- all_conds %>%
  mutate(icd_num = sapply(ICD9CODX, get_icd_num)) %>%
  group_by(DUPERSID) %>%
  summarise(
    # Cancer (140-239) - for exclusion
    has_cancer = as.integer(any(icd_num >= 140 & icd_num <= 239, na.rm = TRUE)),
    
    # Diabetes (250)
    has_diabetes = as.integer(any(icd_num == 250, na.rm = TRUE)),
    
    # Hypertension (401-405)
    has_hypertension = as.integer(any(icd_num >= 401 & icd_num <= 405, na.rm = TRUE)),
    
    # Heart disease (410-429)
    has_heart_disease = as.integer(any(icd_num >= 410 & icd_num <= 429, na.rm = TRUE)),
    
    # COPD and respiratory disease (490-496)
    has_copd = as.integer(any(icd_num >= 490 & icd_num <= 496, na.rm = TRUE)),
    
    # Depression and anxiety disorders (296, 300, 311)
    has_depression = as.integer(any(icd_num %in% c(296, 300, 311), na.rm = TRUE)),
    
    # Arthritis (714-716)
    has_arthritis = as.integer(any(icd_num >= 714 & icd_num <= 716, na.rm = TRUE)),
    
    # Stroke and cerebrovascular disease (430-438)
    has_stroke = as.integer(any(icd_num >= 430 & icd_num <= 438, na.rm = TRUE)),
    
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Calculate total number of chronic conditions per person
chronic_flags <- chronic_flags %>%
  mutate(
    num_conditions = has_diabetes + has_hypertension + has_heart_disease + 
                     has_copd + has_depression + has_arthritis + has_stroke
  )

cat("Chronic condition flags created for", nrow(chronic_flags), "unique persons\n\n")

cat("Condition prevalence in raw data:\n")
cat("Cancer (for exclusion):", sum(chronic_flags$has_cancer), "\n")
cat("Diabetes:", sum(chronic_flags$has_diabetes), "\n")
cat("Hypertension:", sum(chronic_flags$has_hypertension), "\n")
cat("Heart Disease:", sum(chronic_flags$has_heart_disease), "\n")
cat("COPD:", sum(chronic_flags$has_copd), "\n")
cat("Depression:", sum(chronic_flags$has_depression), "\n")
cat("Arthritis:", sum(chronic_flags$has_arthritis), "\n")
cat("Stroke:", sum(chronic_flags$has_stroke), "\n")
```

## Create Medication Counts and Polypharmacy Indicator

Polypharmacy, defined as concurrent use of 5 or more medications, is a known risk factor for adverse health outcomes including hospitalization.

```{r medications}
# Count unique medications per person using NDC codes
med_counts <- all_rx %>%
  group_by(DUPERSID) %>%
  summarise(
    num_rx_fills = n(),
    num_unique_meds = n_distinct(RXNDC, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Create polypharmacy indicator
med_counts <- med_counts %>%
  mutate(polypharmacy = ifelse(num_unique_meds >= 5, 1, 0))

cat("Medication data processed for", nrow(med_counts), "persons\n")
cat("Persons with polypharmacy (5+ medications):", sum(med_counts$polypharmacy), "\n")
cat("Mean unique medications:", round(mean(med_counts$num_unique_meds), 2), "\n")
```

## Process Longitudinal Panel Data

This function extracts and standardizes variables from each longitudinal panel. Some variable names differ slightly across panels, so the function accounts for these variations.

```{r process-function}
clean_panel <- function(df, panel_num) {
  
  cols <- names(df)
  
  # First, add placeholder columns for variables that might not exist
  # This prevents errors when referencing columns that don't exist in some panels
  if (!"RACETHX" %in% cols) df$RACETHX <- NA
  if (!"RACEX" %in% cols) df$RACEX <- NA
  if (!"MARRY1X" %in% cols) df$MARRY1X <- NA
  if (!"EMPST1" %in% cols) df$EMPST1 <- NA
  if (!"RTHLTH31" %in% cols) df$RTHLTH31 <- NA
  if (!"RTHLTH3" %in% cols) df$RTHLTH3 <- NA
  if (!"MNHLTH31" %in% cols) df$MNHLTH31 <- NA
  if (!"MNHLTH3" %in% cols) df$MNHLTH3 <- NA
  if (!"ACTLIM1" %in% cols) df$ACTLIM1 <- NA
  if (!"OBTOTY1" %in% cols) df$OBTOTY1 <- NA
  if (!"OBDTOT1" %in% cols) df$OBDTOT1 <- NA
  
  result <- df %>%
    mutate(
      panel = panel_num,
      
      # Response variable: any hospitalization in Year 1
      hospitalized = ifelse(IPDISY1 >= 1 & IPDISY1 < 99, 1, 0),
      # Multi-class response variable (NEW) -------------------------------------
      hosp_class = case_when(
        IPDISY1 < 0 ~ NA_integer_,
        IPDISY1 == 0 ~ 0L,
        IPDISY1 == 1 ~ 1L,
        IPDISY1 >= 2 ~ 2L
      ),
      
      # Demographics
      age = ifelse(AGEY1X >= 0, AGEY1X, NA),
      female = ifelse(SEX == 2, 1, 0),
      
      race = case_when(
        !is.na(RACETHX) & RACETHX == 1 ~ "Hispanic",
        !is.na(RACETHX) & RACETHX == 2 ~ "White",
        !is.na(RACETHX) & RACETHX == 3 ~ "Black",
        !is.na(RACETHX) & RACETHX == 4 ~ "Asian",
        !is.na(RACETHX) & RACETHX >= 5 ~ "Other",
        !is.na(RACEX) & RACEX == 1 ~ "White",
        !is.na(RACEX) & RACEX == 2 ~ "Black",
        !is.na(RACEX) & RACEX >= 3 ~ "Other",
        TRUE ~ NA_character_
      ),
      
      region = case_when(
        REGION1 == 1 ~ "Northeast",
        REGION1 == 2 ~ "Midwest",
        REGION1 == 3 ~ "South",
        REGION1 == 4 ~ "West",
        REGION1 < 0 ~ NA_character_,
        TRUE ~ NA_character_
      ),
      
      married = case_when(
        !is.na(MARRY1X) & MARRY1X == 1 ~ 1,
        !is.na(MARRY1X) & MARRY1X > 1 & MARRY1X < 9 ~ 0,
        TRUE ~ NA_real_
      ),
      
      # Socioeconomic factors
      insurance = case_when(
        INSCOVY1 == 1 ~ "Private",
        INSCOVY1 == 2 ~ "Public",
        INSCOVY1 == 3 ~ "Uninsured",
        TRUE ~ NA_character_
      ),
      
      poverty_cat = case_when(
        POVCATY1 == 1 ~ "Poor",
        POVCATY1 == 2 ~ "Near Poor",
        POVCATY1 == 3 ~ "Low Income",
        POVCATY1 == 4 ~ "Middle Income",
        POVCATY1 == 5 ~ "High Income",
        TRUE ~ NA_character_
      ),
      
      employed = case_when(
        !is.na(EMPST1) & EMPST1 == 1 ~ 1,
        !is.na(EMPST1) & EMPST1 > 1 & EMPST1 < 99 ~ 0,
        TRUE ~ NA_real_
      ),
      
      # Health status variables
      health_status = case_when(
        !is.na(RTHLTH31) & RTHLTH31 == 1 ~ "Excellent",
        !is.na(RTHLTH31) & RTHLTH31 == 2 ~ "Very Good",
        !is.na(RTHLTH31) & RTHLTH31 == 3 ~ "Good",
        !is.na(RTHLTH31) & RTHLTH31 == 4 ~ "Fair",
        !is.na(RTHLTH31) & RTHLTH31 == 5 ~ "Poor",
        !is.na(RTHLTH3) & RTHLTH3 == 1 ~ "Excellent",
        !is.na(RTHLTH3) & RTHLTH3 == 2 ~ "Very Good",
        !is.na(RTHLTH3) & RTHLTH3 == 3 ~ "Good",
        !is.na(RTHLTH3) & RTHLTH3 == 4 ~ "Fair",
        !is.na(RTHLTH3) & RTHLTH3 == 5 ~ "Poor",
        TRUE ~ NA_character_
      ),
      
      mental_health = case_when(
        !is.na(MNHLTH31) & MNHLTH31 == 1 ~ "Excellent",
        !is.na(MNHLTH31) & MNHLTH31 == 2 ~ "Very Good",
        !is.na(MNHLTH31) & MNHLTH31 == 3 ~ "Good",
        !is.na(MNHLTH31) & MNHLTH31 == 4 ~ "Fair",
        !is.na(MNHLTH31) & MNHLTH31 == 5 ~ "Poor",
        !is.na(MNHLTH3) & MNHLTH3 == 1 ~ "Excellent",
        !is.na(MNHLTH3) & MNHLTH3 == 2 ~ "Very Good",
        !is.na(MNHLTH3) & MNHLTH3 == 3 ~ "Good",
        !is.na(MNHLTH3) & MNHLTH3 == 4 ~ "Fair",
        !is.na(MNHLTH3) & MNHLTH3 == 5 ~ "Poor",
        TRUE ~ NA_character_
      ),
      
      has_limitation = case_when(
        !is.na(ACTLIM1) & ACTLIM1 == 1 ~ 1,
        !is.na(ACTLIM1) & ACTLIM1 == 2 ~ 0,
        TRUE ~ NA_real_
      ),
      
      # Utilization measures
      er_visits = ifelse(ERTOTY1 >= 0, ERTOTY1, NA),
      
      office_visits = case_when(
        !is.na(OBTOTY1) & OBTOTY1 >= 0 ~ OBTOTY1,
        !is.na(OBDTOT1) & OBDTOT1 >= 0 ~ OBDTOT1,
        TRUE ~ NA_real_
      ),
      
      total_exp = ifelse(TOTEXPY1 >= 0, TOTEXPY1, NA)
    )
  
  result <- result %>%
    select(DUPERSID, panel, hospitalized, hosp_class, age, female, race, region, married,
           insurance, poverty_cat, employed, health_status, mental_health,
           has_limitation, er_visits, office_visits, total_exp)
  
  return(result)
}
```

```{r process-panels}
# Process each panel
cat("Processing longitudinal panels...\n\n")

p6_clean <- clean_panel(p6, 6)
p7_clean <- clean_panel(p7, 7)
p8_clean <- clean_panel(p8, 8)
p9_clean <- clean_panel(p9, 9)
p10_clean <- clean_panel(p10, 10)

# Combine all panels
all_panels <- bind_rows(p6_clean, p7_clean, p8_clean, p9_clean, p10_clean)
cat("Combined panel data:", nrow(all_panels), "records\n")
```

## Apply Filters and Merge Data Sources

```{r filter-merge}
cat("Applying study population filters...\n\n")
cat("Starting sample:", nrow(all_panels), "\n")

# Filter to adults only (age 18+)
adults <- all_panels %>% 
  filter(age >= 18)
cat("After restricting to adults (18+):", nrow(adults), "\n")

# Merge chronic condition flags
adults <- adults %>%
  left_join(chronic_flags, by = "DUPERSID")

# Exclude cancer patients
no_cancer <- adults %>%
  filter(is.na(has_cancer) | has_cancer == 0)
cat("After excluding cancer patients:", nrow(no_cancer), "\n")

# Merge medication data
final_df <- no_cancer %>%
  left_join(med_counts %>% select(DUPERSID, num_unique_meds, polypharmacy), 
            by = "DUPERSID")

# Replace NA values with 0 for persons with no recorded conditions/medications
final_df <- final_df %>%
  mutate(
    has_diabetes = ifelse(is.na(has_diabetes), 0, has_diabetes),
    has_hypertension = ifelse(is.na(has_hypertension), 0, has_hypertension),
    has_heart_disease = ifelse(is.na(has_heart_disease), 0, has_heart_disease),
    has_copd = ifelse(is.na(has_copd), 0, has_copd),
    has_depression = ifelse(is.na(has_depression), 0, has_depression),
    has_arthritis = ifelse(is.na(has_arthritis), 0, has_arthritis),
    has_stroke = ifelse(is.na(has_stroke), 0, has_stroke),
    num_conditions = ifelse(is.na(num_conditions), 0, num_conditions),
    num_unique_meds = ifelse(is.na(num_unique_meds), 0, num_unique_meds),
    polypharmacy = ifelse(is.na(polypharmacy), 0, polypharmacy)
  ) %>%
  select(-has_cancer)

# Add multi-class label
final_df <- final_df %>%
  mutate(
    hosp_class_label = case_when(
      hosp_class == 0 ~ "None",
      hosp_class == 1 ~ "Single",
      hosp_class == 2 ~ "Multiple"
    ),
    hosp_class_label = factor(hosp_class_label, levels = c("None", "Single", "Multiple"))
  )

cat("\nFinal analytic dataset:", nrow(final_df), "observations,", ncol(final_df), "variables\n")
```

## Chronic Condition Variables

```{r condition-summary}
cat("Chronic Condition Prevalence:\n\n")

cond_vars <- c("has_diabetes", "has_hypertension", "has_heart_disease", 
               "has_copd", "has_depression", "has_arthritis", "has_stroke")

for (var in cond_vars) {
  n <- sum(final_df[[var]])
  pct <- round(mean(final_df[[var]]) * 100, 1)
  label <- gsub("has_", "", var)
  cat(sprintf("%-15s: %5d (%4.1f%%)\n", label, n, pct))
}

cat("\nNumber of Chronic Conditions:\n")
print(table(final_df$num_conditions))
```

Hypertension is the most prevalent chronic condition at approximately 16%, followed by depression and heart disease. The distribution of multimorbidity shows that a substantial portion of the population has multiple chronic conditions.

## Save Final Dataset

```{r save-data}
dir.create("data/processed", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Modeling file read by the notebooks and the dashboard.
# office_visits is not used as a predictor, so it is left out.
write.csv(final_df %>% select(-office_visits),
          "data/processed/final_for_modeling.csv", row.names = FALSE)

cat("Final dataset saved to data/processed/final_for_modeling.csv\n")
```

# Analysis Methodology

## Exploratory Data Analysis

To examine the relationship between the newly created variables (chronic conditions, polypharmacy) and hospitalization, I calculated hospitalization rates across different subgroups.

### Hospitalization by Number of Chronic Conditions

```{r eda-conditions}
by_conditions <- final_df %>%
  group_by(num_conditions) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    hospitalized = sum(hospitalized, na.rm = TRUE),
    rate = round(hospitalized / n * 100, 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

kable(by_conditions, col.names = c("Chronic Conditions", "N", "Hospitalized", "Rate (%)"))
```

There is a clear dose-response relationship between the number of chronic conditions and hospitalization rate. Individuals with no chronic conditions have a hospitalization rate of approximately 4%, while those with 4 or more conditions have rates exceeding 25%.

```{r plot-conditions, fig.width=9, fig.height=5}
ggplot(by_conditions, aes(x = factor(num_conditions), y = rate, fill = factor(num_conditions))) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(rate, "%")), vjust = -0.3, size = 3.5) +
  labs(
    title = "Hospitalization Rate by Number of Chronic Conditions",
    subtitle = "MEPS Panels 6-10 (2001-2006), Adults without Cancer",
    x = "Number of Chronic Conditions",
    y = "Hospitalization Rate (%)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  ylim(0, max(by_conditions$rate) + 5)
```

### Hospitalization by Polypharmacy Status

```{r eda-polypharmacy}
by_poly <- final_df %>%
  mutate(poly_label = ifelse(polypharmacy == 1, "5+ Medications", "< 5 Medications")) %>%
  group_by(poly_label) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    hospitalized = sum(hospitalized, na.rm = TRUE),
    rate = round(hospitalized / n * 100, 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

kable(by_poly, col.names = c("Polypharmacy Status", "N", "Hospitalized", "Rate (%)"))
```

Individuals with polypharmacy have nearly three times the hospitalization rate compared to those taking fewer than 5 medications.

```{r plot-polypharmacy, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
ggplot(by_poly, aes(x = poly_label, y = rate, fill = poly_label)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(rate, "%")), vjust = -0.3, size = 4) +
  labs(
    title = "Hospitalization Rate by Polypharmacy Status",
    subtitle = "Polypharmacy defined as 5 or more unique medications",
    x = "",
    y = "Hospitalization Rate (%)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  ylim(0, 25)
```

### Hospitalization by Self-Reported Health Status

```{r eda-health}
by_health <- final_df %>%
  filter(!is.na(health_status)) %>%
  group_by(health_status) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    hospitalized = sum(hospitalized, na.rm = TRUE),
    rate = round(hospitalized / n * 100, 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

by_health$health_status <- factor(by_health$health_status, 
                                   levels = c("Excellent", "Very Good", "Good", "Fair", "Poor"))
by_health <- by_health %>% arrange(health_status)

kable(by_health, col.names = c("Health Status", "N", "Hospitalized", "Rate (%)"))
```

```{r plot-health, fig.width=9, fig.height=5}
ggplot(by_health, aes(x = health_status, y = rate, fill = health_status)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(rate, "%")), vjust = -0.3, size = 3.5) +
  labs(
    title = "Hospitalization Rate by Self-Reported Health Status",
    subtitle = "MEPS Panels 6-10 (2001-2006), Adults without Cancer",

    y = "Hospitalization Rate (%)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +

```

The gradient from Excellent to Poor health status shows a strong relationship with hospitalization risk, consistent with findings from the Week 2 analysis.


# Conclusion

## Summary

This week's work expanded the dataset and added clinically relevant variables:

1. **Expanded data scope** - Loaded all five longitudinal panels (6-10) covering 2001-2006, increasing the sample size substantially compared to the Week 2 analysis which used only Panels 6-7.

2. **Integrated multiple data sources** - Combined data from longitudinal files, medical condition files, and prescribed medicine files to create a comprehensive analytic dataset.

3. **Created chronic condition flags** - Derived binary indicators for seven major chronic conditions (diabetes, hypertension, heart disease, COPD, depression, arthritis, stroke) using ICD-9 diagnosis codes.

4. **Created medication variables** - Calculated unique medication counts and polypharmacy indicator from prescription records.

5. **Built final analytic dataset** - Merged all variables and applied study filters (adults only, cancer patients excluded), resulting in a dataset with 25 variables.


# Part B: Transition to Multi-Class Classification

## Rationale for Multi-Class Approach

The binary classification treats all hospitalizations equally, but clinically there are meaningful differences. Single hospitalizations may represent planned procedures or acute events, while multiple hospitalizations often indicate chronic disease complications or readmissions. This section examines the new 3-class response variable.

## Multi-Class Distribution
```{r multiclass-distribution}
cat("Multi-Class Hospitalization Distribution:\n\n")

multiclass_table <- final_df %>%
  filter(!is.na(hosp_class_label)) %>%
  group_by(hosp_class_label) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(percentage = round(n / sum(n) * 100, 1))

kable(multiclass_table, 
      col.names = c("Class", "N", "Percentage (%)"),
      caption = "Distribution of Hospitalization Intensity Classes")
```
```{r fig-multiclass-dist, fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
ggplot(multiclass_table, aes(x = hosp_class_label, y = n, fill = hosp_class_label)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(n, "\n(", percentage, "%)")), vjust = -0.2, size = 3.5) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Hospitalization Intensity Classes",
    subtitle = "MEPS Panels 6-10 (2001-2006), Adults without Cancer",
    x = "Hospitalization Class",
    y = "Number of Adults"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("None" = "#4DAF4A", "Single" = "#377EB8", "Multiple" = "#E41A1C")) +
  ylim(0, max(multiclass_table$n) * 1.15)
```

## Multi-Class by Insurance Status

## Multi-Class by Number of Chronic Conditions
```{r multiclass-conditions}
by_conditions_multi <- final_df %>%
  filter(!is.na(hosp_class_label)) %>%
  mutate(conditions_group = case_when(
    num_conditions == 0 ~ "0",
    num_conditions == 1 ~ "1",
    num_conditions == 2 ~ "2",
    num_conditions >= 3 ~ "3+"
  )) %>%
  group_by(conditions_group, hosp_class_label) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(conditions_group) %>%
  mutate(
    total = sum(n),
    percentage = round(n / total * 100, 1)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(conditions_group = factor(conditions_group, levels = c("0", "1", "2", "3+")))

kable(by_conditions_multi %>%
        select(conditions_group, hosp_class_label, percentage) %>%
        pivot_wider(names_from = hosp_class_label, values_from = percentage),
      caption = "Hospitalization Class Distribution by Number of Chronic Conditions (%)")
```

## Summary Statistics by Hospitalization Class
```{r summary-by-class}
summary_by_class <- final_df %>%
  filter(!is.na(hosp_class_label)) %>%
  group_by(hosp_class_label) %>%
  summarise(
    N = n(),
    Mean_Age = round(mean(age, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    Pct_Female = round(mean(female, na.rm = TRUE) * 100, 1),
    Mean_Conditions = round(mean(num_conditions, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    Pct_Polypharmacy = round(mean(polypharmacy, na.rm = TRUE) * 100, 1),
    Mean_ER_Visits = round(mean(er_visits, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    Median_Expenditure = round(median(total_exp, na.rm = TRUE), 0),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

kable(summary_by_class,
      col.names = c("Class", "N", "Mean Age", "% Female", "Mean Conditions",
```
